title: Roll back a failed invoice posting without changing what the caller sees

blocks.text: Accounts receivable posts each invoice with `InvoicePosting.post(...)`: a row in the ledger, the PDF in the archive, and one database transaction around both. Two things have to hold for the people around it.

The nightly job catches `SQLException` from `post(...)` and retries the invoice when the database reports a serialization conflict (SQLState `40001`); anything else it reports. And last month an invoice in a currency nobody had enabled made the ledger code throw, the transaction stayed open, and the connection pool ran dry an hour later.
`write(...)` already does the work of one posting, commit included. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/InvoicePosting.java`:

items: `post(...)`: begin the transaction and run `write(...)`. Whatever goes wrong, the transaction is rolled back and the caller sees the failure exactly as it was thrown. Keep the method's signature.

blocks.text: The tests hand the posting a ledger, an archive and a transaction that record every call.

cases.says: an invoice that posts cleanly is inserted, archived and committed once, with no rollback
when archiving fails, the transaction is rolled back instead of committed and post() throws
an unchecked failure from the ledger also rolls the transaction back, and the caller gets that same exception
a database failure reaches the caller as the same SQLException, so a retry on its SQLState can run

origin.section: Catching Exception to Rethrow It Keeps the Precise throws Clause

concepts: Rethrowing an effectively final catch (Exception e) parameter throws only the checked exceptions the try block can throw, so the method keeps its precise throws clause and the caller sees the same exception.
